Read documents into a document set

Source: R/documents.R
dragon_documents.Rd

Reads files or web pages, splits them into chunks of about max_words words that never cross a heading, and stores the result as a document set under runs_dir/documents/<name>/. Each chunk keeps the file (or URL) and the section heading it came from, so later answers can say where they came from. This is the first step of the document route: no column mapping, no training yet.

Usage

dragon_documents(
  paths,
  name = NULL,
  runs_dir = dragon_runs_dir(),
  max_words = 170,
  min_words = 35,
  index = TRUE
)

Arguments

paths

Character vector of files, directories, or URLs.

name

Name of the document set, used for the directory. Defaults to the first path's file name, or "documents" for several paths.

runs_dir

Parent directory; the set goes under file.path(runs_dir, "documents", name). See dragon_runs_dir() for why the default is temporary and how to keep sets between sessions.

max_words

Target chunk size in words. Chunks never cross a heading, so most are shorter.

min_words

Sections shorter than this are folded into the previous chunk.

index

Build the retrieval index right away (see dragon_index()), so dragon_ask() works immediately. The first call downloads the small embedding model. FALSE postpones it; retrieval then indexes on first use.

Value

A dragon_documents object: the directory, the name, and the manifest. print() lists the sources; dragon_chunks() returns the chunks as a data frame.

Details

Supported inputs: PDF, HTML, Markdown, plain text, Word (.docx), spreadsheets (.xlsx, .csv, .tsv; one chunk per group of rows, each row written as column: value pairs), directories (walked for those file types), and http(s) URLs (fetched once; the page's text is kept).

Reading the same set again re-reads only files whose contents changed and keeps the other chunks as they were. Files named like a changelog (NEWS, CHANGELOG, ...) or made mostly of version headings are read but flagged, and their chunks are down-weighted when retrieved, because they tend to crowd out the page that actually answers a question. Quoted material (block quotes) and code blocks are marked on each chunk so question generation can skip them.

See also

dragon_ask(), dragon_chunks(), dragon_documents_load(), dragon_documents_list()

Examples

if (interactive()) {
docs <- dragon_documents(c("policies.pdf", "https://example.com/faq"), name = "support")
docs
head(dragon_chunks(docs))
}
